journeys.claim: A person sends one prompt through the real terminal client to a Claude PTY session, sees that exact prompt reflected once, answers one permission request once, and sees the turn finish; the host independently records the prompt and decision.

A person sends one prompt through the real terminal client to a headless Claude session, sees that exact prompt reflected once, answers one permission request once, and sees the turn finish; the host records the prompt once and the provider receives exactly one allow.

A person sends one prompt through the real terminal client to a Codex session, sees that exact prompt reflected once, answers one permission request once, and sees the turn finish; the host records the prompt once and the provider receives exactly one allow.

A real first run on one host makes its replica of another host's agent; with the origin out of reach a fresh client paints the cached chat from its own store with the host away and the composer waiting, keeps a draft, appends the origin's new turn once when the link returns, keeps its rows on screen through a Reset until the rebuilt transcript swaps in, and reconnects by itself when its own daemon restarts, sending the kept draft.

A laptop that has never paired finds a desk on its network: the hosts overlay lists it as found, not paired, with the command that pairs it, and `amux peers` names it by the desk's own host id. Six digits the desk printed, typed once into `amux pair desk`, pair the two and name the desk by that id, and the desk lists the laptop as paired. The client that was running all along shows the desk online and direct, opens the desk's agent, and sends one prompt the desk records once and answers; the person leaves and the client exits cleanly.

Two machines signed in to one account reach each other only through the relay. A second profile on the laptop opens on its own empty fleet. On the default profile the desk's agent answers a prompt; the laptop then signs out, the desk goes away on screen, and a message written then is held on the laptop and never reaches the desk. Signed in again, the chat is current and the held message reaches the desk once.

From the fleet a person creates a Claude agent on the desk and it answers; renames it and the desk lists the same agent under the new name; stops it and the desk lists it exited with its prompt and reply kept; resumes it from the exited composer with a message and the desk lists the same agent live again, each prompt held once; and deletes it, after which neither the fleet nor the desk has it.

On the laptop a person writes to an agent on the desk: text, a twelve-line paste that stands in the sentence as one token, more text, and a review of the diff the desk computed of the agent's working tree, with a comment on one changed line. The desk receives one prompt holding those four in that order, the paste's exact text and the comment on that line, and the review names a patch whose bytes on the desk's disk hash to that name and hold the edit. Opening the chat again shows the tokens as they were sent.

A person asks headless Claude, planning, for work. The plan shows in the chat with its decision in the composer's box and the plan file Claude writes first shows as no step; sent back with a note, a revised plan arrives, and approved, the work runs. Claude receives the plan sent back with that note, then one approval.

A person asks Claude in its own terminal, planning, for work. The plan shows in the chat while it waits and the plan file Claude writes first shows as no step; sent back with a note, a revised plan arrives, and approved, the work runs; the host holds both plans, no step for the plan file, and the reply.

A person puts Codex in plan mode and asks for work. The plan shows in the chat while Codex's turn runs; when it ends the agent needs the person and the plan's decision takes the composer's box. Implement starts the work out of plan mode. A second plan, sent back with a note, comes back revised. Codex is started on the prompt and the note in plan mode and on the implement turn in default mode.

Headless Claude asks three questions. Each option's preview shows beside the options as the selection moves; one question is answered by picking, one by typing under Something else and one is skipped, all are shown for review, and Claude receives one answer holding exactly the two answers. Asked again, the person replies instead, and Claude receives the question refused with those words.

A tool server's form asks for its fields in the order the server wrote them and shows the answers for review before they go; Claude receives the form accepted with exactly those values. Codex asks to let a tool server's call run, then the server asks the person to sign in at a link it names; saying so answers it and Codex receives both answers.

Prompts sent while an agent works queue under the feed. The newest, withdrawn, returns to the composer as a draft and is cleared, and never reaches the host; the other, sent now, goes into the running turn, and the host holds it once.

With the agent's host out of reach, Enter holds the prompt, shown pending until the host is back, and the host never receives it; with the host back, the held prompt goes by itself and the host holds it once.

The link to the agent's host is cut while the host holds a prompt it has not answered: the prompt reads may not have arrived, not not sent. When the link returns it settles without a resend, and the host holds it exactly once.

At a usage limit the composer names the window and when it resets, and a prompt still goes and is answered. Refused its credential, headless Claude's chat puts signing in on the composer's box, naming the host to sign in on; the host holds each prompt once.

For someone who chats in each agent's own terminal, a new agent starts from a form. Started on this machine, the terminal is handed to the new Claude and what is typed there reaches it once, and the leader's s comes back home; started on another machine, the agent runs there and its chat opens, saying its terminal is elsewhere. On a host whose providers are signed out, the form says so on each agent.

From the laptop, a new Claude agent is set to run on the desk, in the desk's repository, on a model only the desk's catalogue offers, in a new worktree. It starts there on that model and answers; the desk's repository lists the worktree on a branch named after the agent. Started again under the same name, the host gives the second agent the next free name, in a worktree of its own on a branch of that name.

In a chat, the leader's b freezes the screen and opens a report on it. A drag with the mouse marks what looks wrong and takes a note of its own, an overall note follows, and Enter writes one bundle into the installation's reports directory: report.json with the marks in cells and both notes, the frozen screen as text, and the profile's dump with this client's parts, every part not captured declared absent with its reason, readable by this user only. Signed in to no account, the client says the report was kept and why it was not sent.

A phone nobody has signed in on offers Sign In on the You tab, and pressing it opens the account service at once, with no page of the app's own between. Closed without finishing, nothing is shown and Sign In is offered again; refused, an alert says so in the account service's words and Try Again asks again; while the browser is up the row says it is signing in, and it comes back signed in where it was pressed with nothing more to press. The account service is asked to sign in and to hand over the account's session. That session's relay, and only it, carries the pairing to a machine that shares no network with the phone: the machine is listed under its own name, its agent opens, and the machine receives the prompt written on the phone exactly once and answers it. Signed out and signing back in, a browser that comes back as another account is named in a question, and Cancel keeps nobody and lets that account's session go.

Signed in to an account that has bought nothing, the relay lists the account's machine and carries nothing to it, so a pairing link through the relay is refused. Bought at the App Store while amux.sh cannot be reached, the purchase is kept and the paywall says it is not confirmed; with amux.sh answering again, Restore Purchases offers the App Store's subscription to amux.sh, which takes it, and the paywall says the account is subscribed. The relay link then reads what the account buys, carries the pairing, and the machine receives the prompt written on the phone exactly once and answers it.

On a phone signed in and paired through the relay, the system's screenshot makes the app offer Report over the frame it froze; the report opens on that frame and takes a note. amux.sh refuses it in its own words and nothing written is lost; Retry hands over the same report and comes back with a receipt. The report that left the phone, read where it crossed into the account service, carries the note and the frozen screen, and the machine lists the agent that screen showed.

The app, saying it draws at an accessibility text size, pairs with a machine on the keypad, opens a Claude agent and sends it a prompt; the permission card it raises is read and answered with Allow once at that size, the machine holds the prompt once and finishes the turn, and the provider receives exactly one allow. At that size every control on Hosts and Settings lies whole across the screen, and the Appearance choices are clear of one another.

With the local network refused, the Hosts tab says so, offers the setting that undoes it and lists no machine; granted, the phone's own browser finds the machine on its network and offers it. The amux://pair link the machine printed, opened from outside the app as the system hands a scanned code over, names the machine before anything is trusted; trusted, the machine is listed under its own name and receives the prompt written on the phone exactly once and answers it.

A phone paired with a machine running two agents is put away. At the machine one agent comes to need the person and the other answers a question. A push built from journeys/fixtures/needs-you.apns names the first: xcrun simctl push shows its notification, and because this simulator never hands a push's payload to an app put away, the debug door hands the same payload to the app's remote-notification handler with the app held in the background, as iOS calls it for a push that wakes the app; the handler brings that one chat current and nothing else: with the machine stopped and the app brought back to the foreground, the named agent's chat holds its ask and the other agent's chat does not hold the answer it gave while the app was away. In the foreground, with the machine running again, the other agent catches up without being named, and the ask answered on the phone reaches the machine, which finishes the turn.

A phone signed in to the account two machines are on pairs with both on its network. Opened for the first time ever, it reaches each with a full handshake; closed and opened again, it reaches each by resuming the last session with its first calls sent as early data and accepted; with one machine restarted while the phone was closed, the next launch still resumes both. After each launch the fleet reads current and the app's link log for that launch is kept beside the run.

Three agents, one of each kind, are mid-turn when amux is killed; they finish their turns into their journals with no daemon, outlive their grace and exit. Any amux command starts amux again under its supervisor, which finds them exited; a newer build is installed under the supervisor and activated; every finished turn is in the store, and resuming the exited agents loses nothing.

retired_phone_journeys.about: Phone journeys written for the app before it ran on one runtime per profile. Each claim of each is either carried by a named step of a current story (story/screen, a screen that story compares) or listed as dropped with why.

journeys.how: Found by the phone's own browser and paired by the printed code with the machine's name and key before trust, with no account (reach-host); the machine away and reached again with nobody pressing anything (leave-and-recover); the local network refused, said so and where it is undone (local-network).

claims.claim: The phone's own browser finds a machine on its network and offers it by name, not paired.
Six digits the machine printed, typed on the keypad, show the machine's name and key before anything is trusted.
Paired with no account anywhere, the phone lists the machine.
The machine's agent opens and answers a prompt.
The machine going away and coming back is reached again with nobody pressing anything.
With the local network refused the phone says so and offers the setting that undoes it.

dropped.claim: The machine lists exactly one paired device afterwards.
dropped.why: The story checks the pairing from the phone's side; the machine's own record of a pairing is pinned by testnet's pairing specs (spec_network a_pairing_window_is_one_shot_attempt_capped_and_expires), not re-checked by a phone story.

journeys.how: A chat drawn from the phone's own store before any host answers (leave-and-recover's fresh client with the origin away, push-wake's pushed chat with the machine stopped).

claims.claim: A chat is drawn from the phone's own store before its host answers.
A pushed chat is drawn with its machine stopped, holding the ask the push named.

dropped.claim: Remembered rows are marked remembered.
dropped.why: The rebuilt fleet has no remembered marking; a host out of reach is said by its away line instead (leave-and-recover/cached-offline).

dropped.claim: The signposts firstCachedFrame, streamConnected and reconciled fire, and no connection is made before one is asked for.
dropped.why: The signposts belonged to the phone's performance suite, which is retired; no story measures them.

dropped.claim: Four remembered rows reconcile to an empty fleet when two unpaired hosts answer through the relay.
dropped.why: The retired journey drove it through the old app's bridge door, which the rebuilt app does not have, and no story re-enacts it on the phone. The remembered-store seeding it needed is gone with it.

journeys.how: Remembered rows kept on screen with the host away and confirmed when it answers (leave-and-recover); every listed agent current again in the foreground (push-wake); a row opened to its chat and the back chevron returning to the fleet (reach-host).

claims.claim: Remembered rows stay on screen with the host away.
Rows are confirmed in place when the host answers, and a new turn appears once.
Every listed agent is current again in the foreground.
A row opens its chat and the back chevron returns to the same fleet.

dropped.claim: Six agents on two machines listed in recency order, with the subtitle '1 need you · 6 agents' and ages like '6m ago'.
dropped.why: The fleet's order and wording are held by the shared view goldens (crates/ui-view/tests/goldens) and the fleet.busy component snapshot rather than a story; no story pairs two machines.

dropped.claim: Edge-swipe back returns to the fleet.
dropped.why: No story swipes; the back chevron is exercised and the swipe is the system's own navigation gesture.

dropped.claim: An empty signed-out fleet.
dropped.why: Not re-enacted by a story; keep-authority/other-account shows an empty fleet for a second account instead.

journeys.how: A chat read and a prompt the host receives exactly once, per kind (conversation-decision stories); the host away said where the composer goes and a message held until it can be sent (leave-and-recover); the changes the host computed opened from the chat (attachment-or-review).

claims.claim: A chat is read and a prompt reaches the host exactly once, for each kind of agent.
The same for headless Claude.
The same for Codex.
With the host away the composer waits and a message is held until it can be sent, then delivered once.
A rewind and Reset keeps rows on screen until the rebuilt transcript swaps in.
An exited agent reads exited and resumes from its composer.
The changes the host computed open from the chat.

dropped.why: Row kinds are held per kind by the chat component snapshots and the shared view goldens (crates/ui-view/tests/goldens); no story streams a film.

dropped.claim: Three refused sends (catching up, unreachable, unanswered) with only 'carry on then' reaching the host.
dropped.why: leave-and-recover holds one message until the host is back; the separate refusal reasons are pinned in the shared client model's tests, not by a phone story.

dropped.claim: A report taken on a left conversation records the draft, sheet and reading position.
dropped.why: The rebuilt report's trace records routes, appearance, type size, account and the frozen instant only; drafts and reading position are not in it.

journeys.how: A permission answered on the phone and the host and provider receiving exactly what was pressed, per kind (conversation-decision stories), at an accessibility size (accessibility) and after a push woke the app (push-wake). The other ask bodies are held by the chat's component snapshots.

claims.claim: A permission answered Allow on the phone reaches terminal Claude once.

dropped.claim: Answers other than Allow once (a deny with a note, a standing grant, a question answered with an option, a plan approved or sent back) checked on the host from the phone.
dropped.why: No story answers them from the phone.
